newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia seen liberalising precious metals sector.
newsitem.headline: Russia seen liberalising precious metals sector.

text.p: The head of Russia's state precious metals and stones quality control chamber said liberalisation of Russia's precious metals market was inevitable, the official Itar-Tass news agency said on Monday.
The agency quoted Valentin Nikitin as saying liberalisation of the market was "not so much the right thing to do as inevitable."
He said any changes would have to be carried out so as not to harm producers, but he gave no details.
Russia maintains strict government control over the production and export of gold, platinum and platinum group and other metals.
The quality control chamber is responsible for ensuring that exported precious metals and gems are certified according to international standards.

Tass quoted government sources as saying Nikitin and two former deputy directors of the recently dissolved Committee for Precious Metals and Stones (Komdragmet) were in the running for leadership of a new Finance Ministry body that would take over part of Komdragmet's export functions.
Nikitin was indirectly quoted as saying that the new body, to be known as the State Fund for Precious Metals and Stones (GosFond), would include the quality control chamber, of which he is chairman.

President Boris Yeltsin in August ordered Komdragmet broken up and its responsibilities divided between the Finance Ministry and the new Industry Ministry, with the latter in charge of metals and gem production and the Finance Ministry in charge of exports.
Tass said a new government order would soon detail the division.
